stem: A facility switches water sources. The new source has nearly the same pH as the old source but a higher EC. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Similar pH means the two sources should behave the same because acidity is the main driver of solution chemistry
Higher EC indicates a changed dissolved-ion load, so review source records before assuming equivalent behavior
Higher EC means irrigation volume should be reduced in direct proportion to the increase in conductivity
Similar pH indicates alkalinity and ion composition are probably unchanged despite the higher conductivity
rationale: Similar pH does not establish equivalent source-water chemistry. A higher EC indicates a changed ionic load and warrants comparison with prior source-water records before management changes are made.
